props.title: Swingers
props.initialSlug: When Vegas calls, the boys swing.

sections.content: Swingers (1996) perfectly captures the swagger and insecurity of mid-90s LA wannabe actors trying to be "money." Jon Favreau's semi-autobiographical script follows Mike (Favreau), a struggling comedian nursing heartbreak while his smooth-talking friend Trent (Vince Vaughn) drags him through Vegas and Hollywood's retro-swing scene. The film launched both actors' careers and established Doug Liman as a director to watch. Its influence echoes through indie comedies like Garden State (2004) and 500 Days of Summer (2009) - relationship films that balance humor with genuine emotional stakes.

sections.content: The film's lasting impact goes beyond its quotable dialogue ("You're so money and you don't even know it"). It helped kickstart the 90s swing revival alongside films like Swing Kids (1993) and inspired a wave of indie comedies about twenty-something male friendship and dating anxiety. The low-budget production ($200,000) and naturalistic dialogue influenced later mumblecore films like Funny Ha Ha (2002) and The Puffy Chair (2005).

Swingers' Las Vegas sequences set a template for "guys night out" films, predating The Hangover (2009) by over a decade. The authentic portrayal of struggling actors in LA would influence everything from Entourage (2004-2011) to La La Land (2016). The film's mix of comedy and melancholy about modern dating resonates through works like High Fidelity (2000) and (500) Days of Summer (2009). SUBHEAD: Impact on Independent Filmmaking

sections.content: The success of Swingers helped establish Miramax's dominance in 90s independent film distribution. Its $200,000 budget and $4.5 million box office proved the viability of micro-budget features, paving the way for films like The Blair Witch Project (1999) and Napoleon Dynamite (2004). The film's DIY production methods - shooting without permits, using real locations, minimal crew - became a blueprint for aspiring filmmakers.
